prompt: You want to Grignard-add to a ketone that has a free OH elsewhere in the molecule. What should you do first?

options.label: Protect the OH (TBS-Cl, imidazole), run the Grignard, then deprotect (TBAF).
Use excess Grignard (one eq is consumed by the OH; one more adds to the ketone).
Reduce the ketone to alcohol first.
Just run the reaction; the Grignard tolerates OH.

explanation: Free OH deprotonates the Grignard (R–MgBr + ROH → R–H + ROMgBr), wasting it entirely. Protecting the OH as a silyl ether (TBS, TBDPS) makes it inert; TBAF cleaves it back after. Excess Grignard works but is wasteful/unclean.
